knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Surface Integral Using Stokes' Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by the closed curve $C$ with positive orientation and parametrization $r(t)=\langle - \cos{\left(t \right)}, - 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}, 1\rangle$ for $t\in [0,2 \pi).$
Given that $F(x,y,z)=\langle - 3 y, 3 x, 0\rangle,$ evaluate the integral

$$
\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm{d}S.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary $C$ with positive orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $S,$ then Stokes' theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=- \cos{\left(t \right)},\quad y=- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)},\quad z=1
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\langle - 3 y, 3 x, 0\rangle \\ & =\langle - 3 \left(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right), 3 \left(- \cos{\left(t \right)}\right), 0\rangle \\ & =\langle 6 \sin{\left(t \right)}, - 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r\prime(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- \cos{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(1\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle \sin{\left(t \right)}, - 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t) & =\langle 6 \sin{\left(t \right)}, - 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\cdot \langle \sin{\left(t \right)}, - 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle \\ & =\left(6 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(\sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(- 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot \left(0\right) \\ & =\left(6 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(6 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right) \\ & =6 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 6 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} \\ & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm dS & =\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi} F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\left(6\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[\left(6 t\right)\right]_{0}^{2 \pi} \\ & =\left(\left(12 \pi\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)\right) \\ & =12 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t) & =\langle 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}, 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\cdot \langle 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}, 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle \\ & =\left(2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot \left(0\right) \\ & =\left(4 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(4 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right) \\ & =4 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 4 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} \\ & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm dS & =\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi} F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\left(4\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[\left(4 t\right)\right]_{0}^{2 \pi} \\ & =\left(\left(8 \pi\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)\right) \\ & =8 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Surface Integral Using Stokes' Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by the closed curve $C$ with positive orientation and parametrization $r(t)=\langle 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}, \sin{\left(t \right)}, 1\rangle$ for $t\in [0,2 \pi).$
Given that $F(x,y,z)=\langle y, - x, 0\rangle,$ evaluate the integral

$$
\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm{d}S.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary $C$ with positive orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $S,$ then Stokes' theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3 \cos{\left(t \right)},\quad y=\sin{\left(t \right)},\quad z=1
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\langle y, - x, 0\rangle \\ & =\langle \left(\sin{\left(t \right)}\right), - \left(3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right), 0\rangle \\ & =\langle \sin{\left(t \right)}, - 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r\prime(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(\sin{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(1\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle - 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}, \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t) & =\langle \sin{\left(t \right)}, - 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\cdot \langle - 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}, \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle \\ & =\left(\sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot \left(0\right) \\ & =\left(- 3 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 3 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right) \\ & =- 3 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} - 3 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} \\ & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm dS & =\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi} F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\left(-3\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[\left(- 3 t\right)\right]_{0}^{2 \pi} \\ & =\left(\left(- 6 \pi\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)\right) \\ & =- 6 \pi\end{aligned}
$$
